title: Brämabühl 15 January 2019 interpreted release and deposit outlines

source.provider: WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF / Zenodo
source.permitted_use: Reuse with attribution under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International.

acquisition.basis: The registered evidence spans the 15 January avalanche occurrence and drone orthophotography acquired one day later; polygon acquisition itself was on 16 January.

normalization_method: Source polygon coordinates copied without reprojection, rounding, simplification, or topology repair.
normalization_software: GeoPandas 1.1.4, Pyogrio 0.13.0, and Shapely 2.1.2 used only for lossless Shapefile-to-GeoJSON serialization.

spatial_coverage.description: Exact aggregate bounds of the registered Wildi and Rüchi source polygons; this is not a surveyed-domain boundary.

detection_limitations: Only positive release and deposition outlines interpreted from a post-event drone orthophoto are registered. The report does not declare a complete survey domain, a detection threshold, or false-negative characterization. Powder-cloud outlines are deliberately excluded.

positional_uncertainty.method: The source report gives no quantified horizontal positional uncertainty for the interpreted outlines.

limitations: Remote-sensing interpretation is qualitative evidence under the avycore contract, not field-validation ground truth.
No quantified horizontal uncertainty or complete surveyed domain is published, so strict IoU and within-uncertainty endpoint metrics are ineligible.
The mapped deposit is the dense-deposition outline; the source also documents a powder component that this engine does not model.
A modern or summer DTM is not the 15 January event-day snow surface; event-day terrain error is unquantified by this dataset.
The scenario records approximate regional new snow and the control trigger, but no event-specific wind vector, release depth, or release-size class.
